units.function: Table-driven authorization regression tests for company reads, settings, branding, lifecycle, export and import across Agent and board identities.
units.dependencyDirection: Express/Supertest requests with fake actors exercise the real companies router while injected services and activity logging expose whether denied calls reach side effects.
units.keyDataModels: Company membership, board roles, local_implicit and instance-admin actors, same-company CEO Agent, portability preview/apply and lifecycle operations.
units.lifecycle: Reject cross-company CEO Agent access; allow selected same-company CEO Agent operations; distinguish non-member, viewer, active member, local implicit admin and non-member instance admin.
units.testAssessment: Approved unsandboxed focused Vitest with isolated PAPERCLIP_HOME passed 12/12. The denial matrix is useful and proves rejected calls stop before mocked service/activity side effects. It intentionally treats every active board member as authorized for archive, hard delete, export and import, and permits a CEO Agent to export/apply imports; no accountable-human approval, data contract, concurrency/idempotency, transaction rollback or audit-completeness cases exist.
units.designRationale: Prevent company ID substitution and cross-company CEO escalation while preserving broad within-company board collaboration and an Agent-safe portability path.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs systematic negative authorization coverage across human, Agent, tenant and deployment-profile actors, but high-risk organization/data lifecycle actions must bind an accountable human, precise authority, approval and evidence.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the operation-by-actor denial matrix and fail-before-side-effect assertions against Company OS commands. Replace Paperclip's positive cases with explicit owner/admin/data-steward roles, verified human responsibility, risk-class approval, export authorization and immutable action/data digests.
units.responsibilityConflict: The suite codifies that an Agent can export and import company state without a matched human approval and that any active member can archive or permanently delete the company. Membership alone cannot establish legal, data-governance or organizational responsibility.

units.function: Monolithic company HTTP router covering listing, statistics, timeline, settings and branding, archive/hard delete, feedback traces, artifacts and full company portability preview/export/import with an in-memory async job facade.
units.dependencyDirection: HTTP actors and Paperclip Cloud environment flow directly into access, company, activity, portability, agent, budget, artifact and feedback services plus database queries; route-local helpers own ZIP parsing, job state, deduplication and response projection.
units.keyDataModels: Company and membership, synthetic local-board principal, default responsible user, free-form CEO Agent role, portability bundle/ZIP, import target/collision strategy, process-memory ImportJobRecord and activity entries.
units.lifecycle: Authorize company actor, parse fully buffered JSON/ZIP, preview/export/import; create company then membership/grants/activity/budget sequentially; mutate settings/branding then log; archive/delete; run optional import jobs in process memory and expire terminal records after one hour.
units.testAssessment: The focused authorization suite passed 12/12 and proves its intended access semantics. Source review found no route-level tests here for durable import recovery, stable errors, ZIP/memory exhaustion, human approval, lifecycle transaction rollback, deletion retention/legal hold, data classification or audit completeness.
units.designRationale: Offer one pragmatic board API for organization administration and portable Cloud/self-hosted transfer, plus a narrowly reduced Agent-safe import mode and lightweight async UX without introducing a durable job subsystem.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs independent organization commands, human/Agent responsibility policy, governed export/import, durable migration jobs and evidence-rich audit across managed-cloud and self-hosted deployments.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as bounded application commands and projections behind Organization, Identity, Authorization, Data Export, Durable Job, Event Store, Audit/Evidence and Approval ports. Retain the useful fail-closed ZIP parsing ideas, explicit safe-mode collision restrictions and cross-company tests, but do not copy this router or its Paperclip DTO/service coupling.
units.responsibilityConflict: A free-form same-company ceo Agent can export/import; any active member can archive, hard-delete, export and import. The local-board synthetic principal can become default responsible owner. None of these high-risk actions requires a verified accountable human, purpose/data contract, exact approval binding or evidence/result digest.

securityFindings: multer.memoryStorage buffers ZIP uploads and the configurable limit can reach 1 GiB; decompression permits at least four times the upload limit, creating material memory and decompression denial-of-service exposure.

Async import returns 202 before deferred target authorization/body validation, stores jobs only in memory, loses them on restart and documents a later 404 as soft success after running was observed; completion and responsibility evidence are therefore ambiguous.
Local duplicate suppression is a per-actor Map scan plus hash of JSON serialization, not durable idempotency; Cloud tenant imports do not receive the same guard.

Company creation, membership, grants, activity and budget policy—and import plus activity—are sequential side effects without a visible enclosing transaction or outbox, allowing partial success and misleading failure state.
Terminal error responses repeat a raw English message in error, message and reason rather than exposing a stable structured code/parameters contract.
